source_text: Hac igitur fidei consolatione gaudentes immineamus coepto operi, et disputationum promissa reddamus; non ambigentes hoc ipsum maximam esse praemii partem, quia in eius dogmatis arce constitimus, quod cum tam multorum livor, sed plurium error oppugnet; tamen ita supra casus evasit ancipites, ut invincibilis cluat possessione victoriae.
pass_a_gloss: Rejoicing therefore in this consolation of faith, let us press upon the work begun, and render the promises of disputations; not doubting that this itself is a very great part of the reward, because we have been stationed in the citadel of that dogma which, though the envy of so many, but the error of more, assails it, has nevertheless so escaped above doubtful falls that it is called invincible by possession of victory.
pass_b_english: Rejoicing, then, in this comfort of faith, let us press on with the work we have begun and fulfill our promise to argue the case. We do not doubt that this itself is a very great part of our reward: we stand in the citadel of a doctrine which, though attacked by the envy of so many and the error of still more, has risen so far above uncertain fortunes that it enjoys an invincible reputation, holding victory in its possession.

choices.why: Opening fides promissionis is the pledge of a promise, not the theological virtue.
Julian's literary pledge to answer, not a covenant-theology 'promise'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
